title: OAuth & Third-Party App Access Governance for Google Workspace
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (enterprise Google Cloud / identity / Gemini enablement).

Google Cloud Console / gcloud / Cloud Identity / Google Admin authored at exact detail from Google public docs; version- or preview-dependent capabilities (SCC tiers, BeyondCorp features, org-policy constraints, VPC-SC behaviors, Gemini Enterprise features) cited or flagged 'verify in your organization', never invented. IaC (Terraform / Cloud Foundation Toolkit) at the pattern level. Automation is Python (gcloud / Cloud Client Libraries) — no hardcoded credentials, no committed service-account keys, no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Control which third-party apps can touch your Google data
problem: Every user who clicks “Allow” on a third-party app grants it OAuth access to Google data — a huge, mostly invisible attack surface. This solution establishes OAuth & app-access governance: inventory connected apps and their scopes, set API access control (trusted/limited/blocked, Marketplace allowlisting, unverified-app blocking), review high-risk scopes and tokens, and stand up an app-vetting/approval workflow — so only trusted apps reach your data.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the OAuth risk model: scopes, connected apps, API access control (trusted/limited/blocked), Marketplace allowlisting, unverified-app blocking, and the vetting flow.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (Workspace super-admin, security/governance stakeholders, risk criteria).

Implementation Guide — inventory connected apps + scopes, classify by risk, configure API access control + Marketplace allowlist + unverified-app block, wire an app-approval workflow, and revoke risky grants — pilot-first.

5 Python tools — assessment/discovery, a configuration or provisioning helper, a validation/report generator, a policy/guardrail check, and a scope/config helper — authentic gcloud / Cloud Client Library automation (read-only or dry-run by default; no credentials or keys in code).
Validation gates (high-risk scopes controlled, unverified apps blocked, approvals enforced) plus Best Practices for ongoing app-access hygiene.
short: Establish OAuth & third-party app-access governance for Google Workspace — app/scope inventory, API access control (trusted/limited/blocked, Marketplace allowlist, unverified-app block), token review, and an app-vetting workflow — so only trusted apps reach your data. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
